content.title: Micro-Gesture Global Rewrite | Trigger, Distributed Disruption, Calm Passage
content.summary: A greenhouse inspector triggers a bench-by-bench water-pressure wave with one counter tap. Preserve the five causal invariants and terminal proof while replacing every source-specific surface.

quick_start.input_format: An ordinary moving environment is established before the trigger. + One small visible gesture is the sole initiating cause. + Consequences propagate in a readable spatial order. + The triggering subject remains identity- and route-stable. + The final frame proves both the traveler and accumulated result.
quick_start.recommended_input: Follow one adult botanical inspector down a busy greenhouse aisle while workers carry trays on both sides. Only the nearest irrigation valves pulse, then a visible water-pressure wave travels down successive benches. Hold the inspector at the dry end marker as every valve settles behind in a readable sequence.
required_anchors: An ordinary moving environment is established before the trigger.
One small visible gesture is the sole initiating cause.
The triggering subject remains identity- and route-stable.
The final frame proves both the traveler and accumulated result.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: A greenhouse inspector triggers a bench-by-bench water-pressure wave with one counter tap. Preserve the five causal invariants and terminal proof while replacing every source-specific surface.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue, or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
